Welcome back! Thirty minutes was all it took, Anthropic published the numbers on its own vanishing junior roles, OpenCode lost API keys to a distillation campaign, and DeepSeek shipped a model that beats Opus while insisting it’s ChatGPT.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Thirty minutes to crack the NSA, fifteen to fix your parents’ TV: One open question cryptographers never answered, and one chore nobody thought was worth the afternoon. Anthropic cut its juniors and pledged 5% of the company: Junior hires fell from 27% to 9%, and the fund arrives with an example use case that names the problem. OpenCode got hacked, and the models investigating it refused to help: Analyzing the attack tripped their safety filters, which Hugging Face already knew. DeepSeek’s new model beats Opus and GPT-5.6, and still thinks it’s ChatGPT: 26 times out of 30, asked the same question. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. Thirty minutes to crack the NSA, fifteen to fix your parents' TV A large share of the web's encryption rests on numbers the NSA handed over in the late 1990s with no explanation of where they came from.  Cryptographers have wondered ever since whether a backdoor was hidden inside them. A legend grew up around it: an NSA employee generated them by scrambling a joke phrase about giving Bob and Jerry a raise. Several Anthropic employees chased that lead and found nothing. Claude solved it in under thirty minutes.  The numbers came from a basic random number generator, seeded from the computer's clock on dates between May 1997 and April 1998. Mid-solve it paused to consider whether it was being tested, rechecked the math, and concluded the result was real. Anthropic says a backdoor now looks much less likely and nobody needs to do anything. The $36,864 bounty goes to the Internet Security Research Group. The same week, someone handed Claude Code the model number of their parents' Xiaomi TV, which had been showing a sponsored ad before you could reach Netflix.  Fifteen minutes later it had found the TV on the Wi-Fi, disabled 25 preloaded packages and written a new launcher from scratch. GM, data enthusiasts! We hope you’re enjoying some sun while you still can! We recently launched [The Latent](https://thelatent.co/), our sister site covering AI. You can sign up for [The Latent Daily](https://thelatent.co/newsletter) to follow the biggest stories in AI.

This week, we’re taking a look at Robinhood Chain activity and perpetuals. We’ll also look at RWA diversity, NFTs, and VC deals. So grab a drink, take a seat, and let’s dive in.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# ==1: RWA Chain Diversity==


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/52ebd6b0-0423-41e2-b813-364a2cd3145d/RWA_Market_Cap_by_Blockchain_Share.png?t=1792420790)
Follow image link: (https://www.theblock.co/data/decentralized-finance/real-world-assets/rwa-market-cap-by-blockchain-market-share)
Caption: 

----------
**Key Insights** provided by The Block Research

* As market cap for RWAs grows, where these assets live becomes increasingly competitive. Ethereum was and continues to be the most dominant chain for RWAs, commanding over 40% of the market cap today.

  * However, Ethereum’s market share is actually down nearly 30 percentage points from a year ago, when it held nearly three-quarters of the market.

* Other competing chains like Solana, BNB, Stellar, and Avalanche have all carved up Ethereum’s position, each gaining 6 percentage points on average in the last 12 months.

  * This diversity supports competition and is likely to continue as RWAs compete. Because tokenization has minimal fees, competition comes down to distribution and adoption. Partnerships with different blockchains to distribute your assets and build integrations are speeding up as more companies look to enter.

* One caveat to remember: it is not enough to simply have the largest market capitalization. Without people actually trading, borrowing, or lending the shares, there’s little real adoption.

* Despite tokenized stock market capitalization surging past $3 billion, only about 10% is actively used in DeFi. As regulators worldwide provide more clarity on tokenizing stocks, adoption of tokenized equities across DeFi venues will continue.
